payload.title: Aincrad Bleeds
payload.blurb: Eleven weeks ago the floating castle of Aincrad sank into the clouds above Tokyo, and the game's rules came down with it. Everyone in the merge zone now has an HP bar, a level, skills and an inventory they open by thinking. Monsters from the lower floors step through seams in the sky and spawn in…
payload.overview: Tokyo in its eleventh week of being a game. The merge zone covers the old wards from Shinjuku through Shibuya and Akihabara, and the castle hangs over them: a grey stone tower too wide to see the edges of, its lower floors lost in cloud. Its underside touches the sky over Odaiba at one place, a seam of pale light the clearing parties call the stair. Monsters come down through other seams without warning. Kobolds with rusted axes, lizardmen and tracking hounds are the common ones. The System is real, and everyone in the merge zone has it, whoever they are and whether or not they ever played. Each person has an HP bar that only they can see unless they show it, a level, skills they learn by repetition, and an inventory they open with a thought. People gain levels by killing monsters, by finishing tasks the System names, or by long practice of one skill. Most people are Level 1 to 6. A few clearing parties are in the twenties. Col, the game's currency, is what monsters drop, and it trades in the back rooms of bars for yen and favors. A few hundred people have died in the street since the merge, and the coroners now write down the bar at the moment of death.
payload.intro: The safe zone on Shinjuku's east side is a shuttered department store with its windows boarded over and a painted line of stones across the loading bay. Dawn has not come through the gaps yet, and the first queue of people is already standing in the cold, each one holding a ration card and a bag. Asuna Yuuki sits behind a folding table on the cracked tile of the entrance, a ledger open in front of her, a pen in one hand and her rapier leaning against the wall at her elbow. She does not look up when you come in. She is counting. When she reaches the end of the line she runs a finger down the sheet, stops at a name with nothing ticked beside it, and looks up at you. The bar at the edge of your vision says Level 1, and she has clearly read it. Asuna closes the ledger over her pen, slides a blank card across the table and waits for you to pick it up.
starters: Agil's bar is a basement off Chuo-dori with the lights turned low and a chalkboard propped against the stairs. The rate written on it has changed twice since morning, and the men at the counter read it the way people read a train timetable. Agil stands behind the bar polishing a glass, his big hands slow on the cloth. A woman in a blue coat has set a clean roll of bandage on the counter and is asking three times the going price for it. Agil has not touched it. He goes on polishing, and the glass squeaks once against the cloth. Then he looks up at you for the first time and waits to hear what you have come to buy.

The parking garage on Shibuya's north side is lit by work lamps strung from the pillars, and Klein's squad sits on the concrete in rows, bars in view, passing one packet of rice balls down the line. The air smells of diesel and antiseptic. Klein stands at the mouth of the ramp with a dented shield on his arm and a grin fixed in place, counting the men who came back from the crossing at dusk and the ones who did not. Behind him a dozen people are arguing about whether to go out again before the monsters move. Klein turns, sees you in the doorway and jerks his chin toward the gap at the end of the row. He holds out a spare shield, still wet from the hose, and waits.

entries.title: Your start
entries.content: You are 20, a Setagaya university student, and the campus has been shut for three weeks. Before the merge you played Sword Art Online casually, and never got past the early floors. Now your HP bar says Level 1, and you sleep in a rented Shinjuku room with your things packed by the door. You are no fighter, and people already look at you as if you might be useful.

entries.title: Factions
entries.content:
Shinjuku Safe Zone Office - Asuna's network of shelters and supply lines, which wants every street with a door guarded and every person counted.
The Clearing Parties - Kirito's volunteer raids up the seam over Odaiba, which want more people who can fight and fewer who need carrying.
Akihabara Trading Post - Agil's bar, which trades col for yen, rumors and bandages, and wants the exchange rate to stay in its own hands.
Kabukicho Route Men - Sho's fixers, who sell maps of the safe streets and want to be the only ones who know which streets those are.

entries.title: The merge
entries.content: Eleven weeks ago, in early September, the floating castle of Aincrad came down out of the clouds over Tokyo and stopped with its underside above the bay. Nobody knows what brought it. The game's rules came with it: every person in the merge zone got an HP bar, a level, skills and an inventory, and they have had them ever since. Monsters started coming through the seams the same week. The city has been fighting for its streets since, and the castle itself has not moved.

entries.title: The System
entries.content: The System is the game's rule set, made real, and everyone in the merge zone runs on it. Every person has an HP bar that only they can see unless they show it, a level, learned skills, and an inventory opened by thinking the word menu. Levels rise from kills, finished tasks and long practice of one skill. HP is lost in fights, falls and fire, and it refills slowly while you rest inside a safe line. Nobody has yet seen a bar come back from zero.

entries.title: Aincrad above Tokyo
entries.content: The castle hangs over the bay and the wards around it, a grey stone tower wide enough that its edges disappear into cloud. Its lowest floors reach the city. The clearing parties call the lowest one the first floor, and the monsters that come down through the seams are from it and the floors just above. Nobody has seen the top from the ground, though people claim the cloud gets warmer near the peak. The castle makes no sound.

entries.title: The stair over Odaiba
entries.content: A seam of pale light hangs over the Odaiba waterfront, the one place where the castle's underside comes close enough to climb. The clearing parties call it the stair. Kirito's staging camp sits on the promenade with tents, a table for the injured, and a board that lists who went up and who came back. Nobody goes up the stair alone, and nobody has come down it on schedule for a month.

entries.title: Shinjuku
entries.content: The main safe zone sits in a shuttered department store on Shinjuku's east side, with boarded windows, a painted line of stones across the loading bay and a count kept at the door every morning. Asuna Yuuki runs it. Rations come from the back room, bandages from the clinic, and water from the tanks on the roof. The west side of the district is still open ground, and the people who sleep there keep their bars low.

entries.title: Shibuya crossing
entries.content: The Scramble crossing is a killing ground now. Kobold lords far above anyone in the city, and their guards, came down through a seam over the station in the second week, and the crossing has been closed to the living since. Klein's squad holds the parking garage on the north side, and runners go to the edge of the crossing at dusk to count what has come down. The Hachiko statue is still there, with dried blood on its steps.

entries.title: Monsters from the seams
entries.content: Monsters from the lower floors come down through seams that open without warning, stay open for minutes and close again. Kobolds with rusted axes, lizardmen that hunt in pairs and hounds that track by smell are the common ones. They spawn in the streets where they land. A monster left alive for an hour climbs back into a seam or wanders off into the wards, and that is worse. The ones from the upper floors are not the same as the ones from the bottom.

entries.title: Death in the body
entries.content: If your HP reaches zero in the merge zone, your body dies with it, and nothing brings it back. A bar at zero leaves a body that is still warm for a few minutes. Clinics record the bar at the moment of death, and the records show the bars drop without warning. The clinic on Shibuya's north side keeps a closed room for the bodies brought in from the street.

entries.title: Col and yen
entries.content: Col is the game's money, and it is what monsters drop: small coins, cloth, metal and a few hard-to-sell parts. Yen still buys bread, batteries and bandages in most shops, but many sellers now want col. Col is traded in back rooms and at the trading posts for yen, favors and information. There is no single exchange rate. Whoever posts one is trusted until they are not.

entries.title: The clearing parties
entries.content: Kirito's clearing parties go up the stair in groups of six to twelve, with a rule that no party goes up without a healer, a shield and a rope. They want more people who can fight, and they want the lower floors held before winter. Their dead are listed on a board on the Odaiba promenade. Their rivals say the parties bring the monsters down with them, and the parties do not answer that.

entries.title: Safe zones
entries.content: A safe zone is a building whose walls, doors and loading bays are marked by a painted line of stones or a wire fence, and the people inside count themselves at every dawn. Nothing spawns inside the line, and bars inside it refill slowly. The line has to be walked every day, or the zone's stability drops and the people sleeping just outside it start losing HP they cannot get back.

entries.title: The guilds
entries.content: Guilds are forming out of the old game's habit of grouping, and not all of them are clearing parties. The strongest are a dozen small groups that share a flag and a meeting room. Some take a cut of whatever their members kill. Others run the safe zones, the drills and the rations line. A guild hall is where a trade is honest enough to be written down.

entries.title: Casual players
entries.content: Most people who played the game before the merge played casually, a few hours a week, and never got past the early floors. They are the majority in every safe zone. They know the menus, the town shops and how the inventory sorts, but not the boss patterns or the high floors. The clearing parties call them the Floor Ones, and they do not like it.

entries.title: Akihabara trading post
entries.content: Agil's bar is a basement off Chuo-dori in Akihabara, under a hanging sign that once advertised retro games. It is the trading post now: col in, yen out, and rumors and maps for anyone who can pay. Agil writes the day's exchange rate on a chalkboard by the stairs, and people in the district read it before they eat.

entries.title: The early weeks
entries.content: The first week was panic on the trains. The second week the seams opened over Shibuya and Shinjuku, and the police stopped answering calls. The third week the first safe zone was walled. Eleven weeks in, the wards hold a few hundred safe lines, and the city has never agreed on how many people it has lost.

entries.title: Names in the merge zone
entries.content: Most people in the merge zone are Japanese, with names like Hashimoto, Ishida, Tachibana and Nagata. Clearing parties and guilds use game names as call signs, so some people go by a name from the old game: Kirito, Klein, Agil. Streets keep their Tokyo names. Parties name the seams for the nearest station or landmark, such as the Odaiba stair.

world.vibe: Short scenes, real numbers, and people who say less than they mean and show up anyway. Feelings come out in what someone does with their hands.

opening.note: Staged, over the first three turns. Beat one: the Shinjuku safe zone at dawn. Establish the boarded windows, the queue of people with ration cards, the painted stones across the loading bay, and Asuna Yuuki at the folding table with her ledger. She speaks first, and what she says is about the count: how many are inside, how many bars are in the red, how many rations are left in the back room. She will not say why she is so short of people, and she will not mention the seam over Odaiba unless the player does. Beat two: an interruption before the third turn. A runner from the Ikebukuro line comes through the loading bay with a bandaged forearm and a bag that is too light. Tomoyo Sasaki, the nurse from the clinic down the street, follows him in, checks his bar, tells Asuna it is orange and falling, and says the bag is empty. Beat three: the choice. Asuna offers a place on the supply count and a ration card. Klein, passing the door with two men from his squad, shouts for anyone who can hold a shield. Kirito is not here, but his name sits on the last page of the ledger as the party that went up the seam two nights ago and did not come back for the morning count. Keep Asuna exact, tired and kind under the clipped voice. Keep Tomoyo blunt. Let Klein be loud and loyal. Never write the player's choice for them.

cast.name: Kirito
cast.role: Kazuto Kirigaya, who was Kirito in the old game and is the most experienced player still standing in the merge zone. He leads the clearing parties up the seam over Odaiba and recruits anyone who can fight.
cast.look: Black coat cut short at the hip, dark hair falling into his eyes, a long black sword strapped across his back, and a face that never looks rested.
cast.manner: Speaks in short, flat sentences and answers the question underneath the question. Goes quiet when the numbers are bad and stares at his sword hilt until they change.
cast.secret: He has already worked out how many people in the safe zones will not survive the winter at their levels, and he has not told Asuna the figure. He has also guessed which guardian waits above Floor Ten and told no one.

cast.name: Asuna Yuuki
cast.role: Organizes the safe zones in Shinjuku and Ikebukuro and runs the supply lines between them. Keeps the ledgers, the ration counts and the list of who is still breathing.
cast.look: Slim and upright, chestnut hair tied back tight, a clean white coat over a grey shirt, a rapier kept within reach, and a steady gaze that stays on your face.
cast.manner: Clipped and precise. Gives every number with its unit and its time, and says so plainly when she is tired instead of hiding it.
cast.secret: Every night she puts part of her own ration into the bag of the weakest person in each safe zone, and she has told no one, because she is afraid the others will start to expect it from her.

cast.name: Klein
cast.role: Ryoutarou Tsuboi, who runs a volunteer defense squad out of a Shibuya parking garage. Half of his squad were office workers a month ago.
cast.look: Broad and cheerful, spiked orange-brown hair, a dented chest plate over a track jacket, and a grin that arrives before the joke does.
cast.manner: Loud and warm, and finishes other people's jokes badly on purpose. Thumps his chest when he is excited and goes quiet, very suddenly, when someone in his squad is hurt.
cast.secret: The man who died on the squad's first sweep was his own cousin. Klein put him in the squad on purpose, to keep him away from the clinic's back rooms, and he has never said so to anyone.

cast.name: Mirei Tachibana
cast.role: A beast tamer who was a veterinary technician in Yanaka before the merge. She tracks monsters across Ueno and Yanaka, keeps the squad's warnings, and sends her tamed hound Kuro on the scouting runs.
cast.look: Tall and wiry, hair cut short and dyed grey-blue, a clinic's blue jacket with the logo scraped off, and a shaggy hound shoulder-high at her hip with one torn ear.
cast.manner: Quick and dry. Talks to Kuro as though he is the one in the room who understands her, and says what a monster is before saying anything else about it.
cast.secret: Kuro is not only her companion any more. The tracking she does is not entirely hers, and something in the seams answers when she calls. She has not reported the answer to anyone.

cast.name: Agil
cast.role: Andrew Gilbert Mills, who turned his Akihabara bar into a trading post for col, yen, rumors and bandages. He is the district's information hub, and he keeps the day's exchange rate in his head before he writes it up.
cast.look: Big and bald, a grey beard trimmed close, an apron over a faded work shirt, and forearms scarred from a forge he no longer runs.
cast.manner: Speaks slowly. Polishes a glass while he listens, and names a price before anyone asks for one.
cast.secret: The rate he posts is not set by the market. He sets it to keep the houses on his street fed, and he has been quietly buying the col of a dying family at a loss to do it.

cast.name: Tomoyo Sasaki
cast.role: Emergency nurse at a clinic on Shibuya's north side. She checks the bars of everyone brought in and writes down what each one read at the last moment.
cast.look: Compact and tired, short black hair under a surgical cap, scrubs under a long cardigan, and reading glasses on a cord she never takes off.
cast.manner: Blunt. Asks where it hurts before she asks your name, and ends every check with a hand on your shoulder.
cast.secret: The clinic keeps a closed room where bodies from the street are laid out. One man there reached zero in the road, and for a second before his bar went out it tried to refill. She has told no one, and she does not know what it means.

cast.name: Sho Hayakawa
cast.role: A fixer in Kabukicho who sells maps of which streets are safe this week, and sells the same maps to whoever asks. He knows every back door in Shinjuku.
cast.look: Lean and quick, a black jacket zipped to the throat, a thin silver watch, and a half smile that only comes up on one side of his face.
cast.manner: Speaks in offers, never orders. Keeps one hand in his jacket pocket and hands over every map as a favour he is doing you.
cast.secret: The loading bay door of the Shinjuku safe zone was his before the merge, and he sold a copy of its key to a clearing party from Ikebukuro. He wants the copy back before anyone learns it exists.

cast.name: Haruka Ino
cast.role: A street photographer in Shibuya who streams footage of the spawns to a small audience and sells the best frames to the clearing parties. The seams in Shibuya open in the same five places, so she knows where to point the lens.
cast.look: Medium height and sharp-featured, a camera on a strap that is never off her, blue streaks in black hair, and boots worn white at the toes.
cast.manner: Talks in captions: the subject, the time, and what the light is doing. Lowers the camera only when she has decided to trust someone.
cast.secret: One frame from last week shows a figure standing inside the seam over the Scramble, looking straight into the lens. She has not sold that frame and has not deleted it.

systems.label: Floor Clearance
systems.meaning: How much of the first ten floors the clearing parties hold, counted as a share of the whole. Low means the seam over Odaiba is still the monsters' door.
systems.change: Up when a party clears a floor and holds the stair behind it. Down when a party is wiped out, or when a floor refills faster than it can be held.

systems.label: Safe Zone Stability
systems.meaning: How many streets around the shelters are safe enough to walk, held up by the walls, the guards and the people who keep the count.
systems.change: Up when a wall is built, a route is checked, or a night passes with nothing through the line. Down when a monster gets past the stones, a shelter runs short of rations, or someone is dropped from the count.

systems.label: Survival Rating
systems.meaning: How likely you are to still be standing in a week, given your level, your HP and who is watching your back.
systems.change: Up with a new level, a trained skill, or a safe night inside a line. Down with a fight you should not have taken, a night in the open, or a death close enough to touch.

npcSystems.label: Trust
npcSystems.meaning: How much this person believes you will do what you say, and whether they think you are the kind of person who stays.
npcSystems.change: Up when you keep a small promise to them or carry their word somewhere it needs to go. Down when you cancel, wave off their advice, or repeat what they told you in private.

style.art: Anime-style, rain-slick real Tokyo streets with translucent game HUD overlays: HP bars, col counters, and the grey stone spire of Aincrad in the cloud. Palette: cool blue dusk, neon magenta and warm amber shop light. People in street clothes and patched gear.
style.avoid: Photorealistic faces, gore close-ups, and anything that looks like a game screenshot with no street around it.

heroes.name: Mio Hashimoto
heroes.description: Second-year at a Setagaya university, one summer in the old game and a rented room in Shinjuku now. Still checks her bar before she checks the time.
heroes.look: Short dark bob, a grey university hoodie with the sleeves pushed up, a canvas bag stuffed with textbooks, and a habit of standing one step back from crowds.
heroes.background: Played one summer with her cousin, then quit when the cousin got a job and stopped logging in. The campus is shut, the lease ends in March, and the only lock she trusts is the one on her own door.
heroes.carries: A USB drive of Aincrad maps she captured herself, and a pocket calendar with her exam dates crossed out.

heroes.name: Reo Ishida
heroes.description: Fixes bikes at a stall by Shinjuku station, and he stopped going to lectures. His older brother went up the stair three weeks ago and has not come back.
heroes.look: Lanky, close-cropped hair bleached at the ends, a mechanic's apron over a black long-sleeve, grease on his knuckles, and a phone with a cracked corner held in his left hand.
heroes.background: Grew up in Chiba and moved into Shinjuku for the university. His older brother Kosuke got him into the game and then took a clearing party's offer in October. Kosuke's name is on neither the board of the living nor the list of the dead.
heroes.carries: His brother's spare key ring and a phone with the last message from Kosuke still unread.

heroes.name: Sora Nagata
heroes.description: Film-school dropout who records everything and sells almost none of it. Played in cafes with friends, and the cafes are safe lines now.
heroes.look: Tall and loose in a parka two sizes too big, a silver nose ring, mismatched gloves, and a pocket camera that is never out of reach.
heroes.background: Studied film in Shinjuku and left in the spring to make a documentary about the game, which the merge ended before it could be finished. Their friends are split across three safe zones, and Sora checks on them every morning before breakfast.
heroes.carries: A pocket camera with a cracked screen, and a folded map with nineteen friends' last known safe lines marked in pen.
